by_construction: Labels have zero effect; tau affects only the opaque comparator, not the track-record reader. The source policy is shared across all32 claims and marginalized jointly.
case: Revealed pools distinguish selection-biased from uniform source policies.
check: Exact binomial enumeration under each truth: at least25% of revealed pools have selection-probability change >.1 between s=.5 and s=0. This directly checks source learnability rather than reusing the parent pooled .5/1 likelihood-ratio gate.
choices: Use tau1 once; original three tau strata cannot supply a causal track-reader contrast. Score every prefix1..64 of the same64-record training trajectory and same32 new claims.16 whole-world blocks,32 balanced makers per world.
endpoint: First sampled length with absolute whole-world mean excess capture <=.05 under h0. Also report earliest length for which every later sampled length stays within the bar; allow unavailable crossings and nonmonotonicity.
inference: descriptive; fresh whole-world seeds; no confirmation or human inference
known_answers: Inherited exact controls plus extended log-marginal odds against 60-digit decimal arithmetic, fixed observation prefixes and unchanged coarse U1 readouts.
probe: Both endpoint settings, one excluded world each; one setting repeats with independent identity; all three passes <=1800 CPU seconds.
question: At what training length does learning the shared source policy bring excess false-hypothesis probability within .05 of the transparent reader?
reservation: 1.5 times measured largest per-world cost per pass plus measured overhead and 10 seconds per pass; additional 10-second parent overhead; cumulative caps include probes and failures.
routes: Sounding Line U1: source-model observables for co-writing tests.
selected_from: verified primary only; no texture descendant
uncertainty: Whole-world standard errors at every length; 16 blocks, not256 false-truth makers, determine uncertainty. Crossing is a descriptive grid estimate, not a confidence-certified sample requirement.
